context: Before defining protocols, compare at least four materially different implementations: a conventional SQL adapter, a dataframe/expression-family adapter, h2odb benchmark execution, and read_primitives execution, plus cloud lifecycle behavior where relevant. Build a capability matrix and classify semantic sameness versus genuinely different operations. Type consumers against the smallest capability they need. Preserve compatibility methods and registration; reduce type suppressions only when the underlying mismatch is removed.
description: PlatformAdapter currently aggregates ten mixins while benchmark implementations expose incompatible run_benchmark and execute_query signatures that are suppressed as intentional LSP violations. Define narrow capability protocols based on real consumer needs while preserving the repository-required PlatformAdapter facade and @register_platform contract. This extends rather than repeats the completed physical adapter-base modularization and unified-interface work.

anti_patterns.dont: Create one protocol with every optional adapter method.
anti_patterns.why: That reproduces the god-interface and hides real capabilities.

anti_patterns.dont: Expand global type exclusions after migration.
anti_patterns.instead: Use strict islands and reduce suppressions as contracts become valid.
anti_patterns.why: That would silence rather than repair substitutability defects.

anti_patterns.dont: Rename specialized operations merely to make signatures look uniform.
anti_patterns.why: Syntactic uniformity can conceal semantic incompatibility.

preserves.behavior: Existing third-party adapter subclasses retain a compatibility path.
New SQL platforms still subclass PlatformAdapter and register with @register_platform.
Platform SDK imports remain lazy and registry discovery remains import-safe.
Specialized benchmark operations are not forced into semantically false uniform signatures.

prior_art.concept: Cohesive base modules produced by the completed adapter-base refactor.
Completed physical modularization with facade preservation.
Completed SQL and dataframe interface unification attempt.
